scopes.description: Whether the submission evidences correct mastery of the OST, North Star / metric-tree, and RICE frameworks this Sprint 2 task is built on.
scopes.requirement: Command of core product strategy and prioritization frameworks

examples: Outcome node: 'Raise week-1 module-completion rate from 34% to 55%' instead of 'boost engagement'
Solution bet 'in-app streak reminders' nested under opportunity 'learners lose momentum after the first session'
binary_points.dense_query: opportunity solution tree measurable behavioural outcome hierarchy opportunities solution bets
binary_points.description: Opportunity Solution Tree has a specific, measurable behavioural outcome and a sound outcome to opportunity to solution hierarchy
binary_points.keywords_query: opportunity solution tree outcome measurable opportunity solution bet hierarchy nested
quality_checks: Outcome is quantified and measurable, not an aspiration
Three distinct levels (outcome, opportunities, solution bets) are present and correctly nested
No solution bet is placed at the outcome or opportunity level
binary_points.evaluation_criteria: The top of the tree is a specific, measurable change in learner behaviour (a quantified target), NOT a vague goal like 'improve engagement'. The three levels are distinct and correctly nested: opportunities sit under the outcome and solution bets sit under specific opportunities. YES when the outcome is measurable and the three-level hierarchy is correct; NO when the outcome is vague or opportunities and solutions are conflated onto one level.

examples: NSM = 'learners completing at least one graded milestone per week', justified as a precursor to retention
Write-up explicitly rejects 'total logins' as a vanity metric
binary_points.dense_query: north star metric leading indicator learner value not vanity metric
binary_points.description: North Star Metric is a leading indicator of genuine learner value rather than a vanity metric
binary_points.keywords_query: north star metric NSM leading indicator vanity enrollments logins value
quality_checks: NSM is a leading value indicator, not a lagging or raw-activity count
The write-up explains why it captures real learner value
Enrollments, signups, or logins are not used as the NSM
binary_points.evaluation_criteria: The NSM captures the core value delivered to a learner genuinely progressing through the program and is a leading indicator of that value, NOT a vanity metric such as enrollments, logins, or signups. YES when the NSM plausibly leads real learner progress and the write-up justifies why; NO when it is a raw activity or registration count with no link to progression or value.

examples: Inputs: session frequency, module-completion rate; Lagging: 30-day retention, churn; Guardrail: support-ticket rate to catch frustration
Guardrail 'average time-to-complete' flags a solution that lifts completion by trivializing content
binary_points.dense_query: metric tree input drivers lagging outcome guardrail metric churn
binary_points.description: Metric tree is correctly layered into input, lagging outcome, and guardrail metrics
binary_points.keywords_query: metric tree input lagging guardrail churn business outcome layers
quality_checks: 3-4 input metrics, 1-2 lagging outcome metrics, and at least 1 guardrail are present
The guardrail detects a real harm or side-effect, not just another driver
Lagging metrics connect to churn and business outcomes
binary_points.evaluation_criteria: Beneath the NSM the tree shows 3-4 input metrics that drive it, 1-2 lagging outcome metrics that confirm it (connected to churn and business outcomes), and at least 1 guardrail metric that would reveal harm elsewhere in the product. Each metric is in the correct layer. YES when all three layers exist with the required counts and the guardrail genuinely detects a side-effect; NO when a layer is missing, counts are wrong, or the 'guardrail' is just another input driver.

examples: 'Reach approximately 400 learners/quarter because it only touches new cohorts; Confidence 60% - no A/B data yet' shown before the score
Effort estimated in person-weeks and divided into the product, not guessed as 'low'
binary_points.dense_query: RICE reach impact confidence effort per-component reasoning calibrated confidence
binary_points.description: RICE framework is applied correctly with per-component reasoning and honestly calibrated Confidence
binary_points.keywords_query: RICE reach impact confidence effort reasoning score calibration uncertainty
quality_checks: Final score equals Reach x Impact x Confidence / Effort, not an ad-hoc ranking
Reasoning precedes each component value
Confidence varies across bets and is lowered where evidence is weak
binary_points.evaluation_criteria: Each bet is scored as Reach times Impact times Confidence divided by Effort, the reasoning for every component is shown before the final number, and Confidence expresses genuine uncertainty (it varies across bets and is lowered where evidence is thin). YES when the RICE arithmetic and per-component logic are sound and Confidence is calibrated; NO when only final scores appear or Confidence is uniformly high.

scopes.description: Whether each Sprint 2 artifact (OST, MVP scope, roadmap, RICE backlog) is actually produced to the brief's specific constraints and edge cases.
scopes.requirement: Deliverables built to spec with hard constraints honored

examples: Opportunity annotated '(Sprint 1 interview #4: learners abandon after an unclear first task)'
Each solution bet names the specific opportunity it sits under
binary_points.dense_query: opportunity tree traceable sprint 1 research insight no floating solution
binary_points.description: Opportunity Solution Tree is fully traceable to Sprint 1 research with no floating solution bets
binary_points.keywords_query: traceable sprint 1 research insight opportunity solution floating orphan
quality_checks: Every opportunity references a concrete Sprint 1 insight
No solution bet floats free of an opportunity
Traceability is explicit in the artifact, not merely implied
binary_points.evaluation_criteria: Every opportunity node cites at least one specific Sprint 1 research insight, and every solution bet connects upward through a specific opportunity back to that research - there are no orphan or floating nodes. YES when every node is traceable end-to-end; NO when any opportunity lacks a research citation or any solution cannot be traced back to an insight.

examples: Must Have limited to 3 items; Should/Could/Won't buckets populated; a paragraph 'What we are explicitly not building this MVP and why'
Won't Have list names deferred bets rather than leaving them silent
binary_points.dense_query: MVP scope MoSCoW must have three items not doing statement
binary_points.description: MVP Scope Doc applies MoSCoW with a Must Have list of no more than 3 items and an explicit not-doing statement
binary_points.keywords_query: MVP MoSCoW must should could won't three items not doing scope
quality_checks: Must Have list holds 3 items or fewer
All four MoSCoW categories are used
An explicit written 'not doing' statement is present
binary_points.evaluation_criteria: The doc sorts scope into Must / Should / Could / Won't Have, the Must Have list contains no more than 3 items, and it includes a written statement of what is explicitly NOT being built. YES when all four MoSCoW buckets are used, Must Have is 3 items or fewer, and the 'not doing' statement is present; NO when Must Have exceeds 3 or the explicit 'won't do / not doing' statement is missing.

examples: Week 2 learning goal 'Do learners engage with streak reminders?'; success signal 'at least 40% of nudged learners return within 24h'
Milestones tied to validation checkpoints rather than ship dates
binary_points.dense_query: product roadmap learning goal success signal validation checkpoint per week
binary_points.description: 4-Week Roadmap milestones each carry a learning goal and an observable success signal
binary_points.keywords_query: roadmap learning goal success signal validation milestone week checkpoint
quality_checks: Each milestone states a question to be answered (learning goal)
Each milestone states a specific observable success signal
The roadmap is learning/validation oriented, not a feature-by-week timeline
binary_points.evaluation_criteria: The roadmap is organized around what will be validated and learned each week; every milestone has both a learning goal (a question answerable by the end of that week that cannot be answered now) and a success signal (a specific observable indicator the milestone was achieved). YES when every milestone has both a learning goal and a success signal; NO when it is a list of features/deliverables by week or milestones lack either element.

examples: Five bets, each with a Reach/Impact/Confidence/Effort breakdown followed by the computed score
Backlog bets are the ones surfaced as solution bets in the OST, not fresh ideas
binary_points.dense_query: RICE backlog top five solution bets component reasoning from opportunity tree
binary_points.description: RICE backlog scores exactly the top 5 solution bets with per-component reasoning shown
binary_points.keywords_query: RICE backlog top 5 solution bets reasoning score opportunity tree
quality_checks: Exactly five solution bets are scored
Per-component reasoning is shown before each score
Backlog bets trace to the OST's solution bets
binary_points.evaluation_criteria: The backlog carries exactly the top 5 solution bets from the Opportunity Solution Tree and scores each with all four RICE components' reasoning shown before the number - not merely a ranked list of final scores. YES when exactly 5 bets each show component reasoning and trace back to OST solution bets; NO when the count is wrong, scores appear without reasoning, or the bets are newly invented rather than drawn from the tree.

scopes.description: Whether the Tech Stack Mapping and metric measurement are grounded in how Sprints.ai actually works, with feasibility and unknowns validated.
scopes.requirement: Technical literacy and platform-grounded metric validation

examples: A table with rows Delivery (LMS/frontend), Data (progress DB/warehouse), Analytics (product-analytics tool), Integrations (auth, payments, video)
A high-level architecture sketch that a PM could read at a glance
binary_points.dense_query: tech stack mapping course delivery data storage analytics integrations high level
binary_points.description: Tech Stack Mapping covers delivery, learner-data, analytics, and integrations at an accurate high level
binary_points.keywords_query: tech stack delivery data analytics integrations platform mapping overview
quality_checks: All four areas (delivery, learner data, analytics, integrations) are covered
Depth is high-level and wide, not an unnecessary deep dive
The described stack is technically plausible for a learning platform
binary_points.evaluation_criteria: A structured overview maps how Sprints.ai currently works across all four areas: how courses are delivered, where learner-progress data is stored and accessed, which analytics tools are in use, and which third-party integrations already exist - wide rather than deep. YES when all four areas are covered accurately at a high level; NO when any area is missing or the mapping is technically implausible for a learning platform.

examples: 'Module-completion rate - tracked in the learner-progress DB'; 'Time-to-first-value - NOT currently instrumented (tracking gap)'
A metric-tree column 'How measured today / gap'
binary_points.dense_query: metric measured on platform tracking gap instrumentation flagged
binary_points.description: Each metric is annotated with how it is measured today and unmeasured metrics are flagged as tracking gaps
binary_points.keywords_query: metric measured tracking gap instrumentation platform Sprints not measured
quality_checks: Every metric has a measurement note
Unmeasured metrics are explicitly labelled as tracking gaps
Measurement sources reference the real platform, not a generic tool
binary_points.evaluation_criteria: For every metric in the metric tree the submission notes how it is currently measured on Sprints.ai, and any metric not currently tracked is explicitly flagged as a tracking gap. YES when every metric carries a measurement note and unmeasured ones are labelled tracking gaps; NO when the measurement source is omitted or missing instrumentation is silently ignored.

examples: 'Recommendation engine deferred - requires an event pipeline we do not currently have'
MVP bets confirmed buildable on the existing LMS plus analytics stack
binary_points.dense_query: solution feasibility existing infrastructure no dependency on missing infra
binary_points.description: Proposed solutions are checked against existing infrastructure feasibility
binary_points.keywords_query: feasibility infrastructure existing dependency deferred infra buildable
quality_checks: Solutions are cross-checked against the tech stack map
Infra-heavy bets are flagged or deferred, not silently assumed
No Sprint-3 dependency rests on non-existent infrastructure
binary_points.evaluation_criteria: The scoping explicitly ensures no proposed solution depends on infrastructure that does not exist or would take months to build; bets are checked against the mapped stack for feasibility. YES when solutions are tied to what the mapped stack can support and infra-heavy bets are flagged or deferred; NO when bets assume capabilities the tech map shows are absent, with no flag.

examples: 'Assumption: product analytics run on a third-party tool - could not confirm which; flagged for mentor'
An 'Open questions / assumptions' section within the tech-stack overview
binary_points.dense_query: flag assumptions where clarity missing tech stack open questions
binary_points.description: Areas lacking clarity are explicitly flagged as assumptions rather than asserted as fact
binary_points.keywords_query: assumption flagged unclear open question could not confirm tech stack
quality_checks: Unverified claims are labelled as assumptions
At least one open question or assumption is surfaced in the tech map
Assumptions are specific, not a blanket disclaimer
binary_points.evaluation_criteria: Where the intern could not get clarity (for example on data storage or a specific integration), the gap is flagged and the assumption made is stated explicitly, instead of presenting a guess as verified fact. YES when uncertainties are labelled as assumptions; NO when unknowns are stated as facts or omitted.

scopes.description: Whether the write-ups justify tradeoffs, descoping, and the alignment-sync decision in clear, defensible language.
scopes.requirement: Clear tradeoff reasoning and stakeholder communication

examples: 'Pursuing streak reminders wins fast retention lift for low effort; we give up depth work on assessment quality this sprint.'
Rationale names an opportunity cost, not only the benefit
binary_points.dense_query: RICE tradeoff rationale gain give up two sentences opportunity cost
binary_points.description: Each RICE bet has a two-sentence tradeoff rationale naming what is gained and what is given up
binary_points.keywords_query: tradeoff rationale gain give up opportunity cost two sentence bet
quality_checks: Each of the 5 bets has a tradeoff rationale
Rationale names both a concrete gain and a concrete give-up
Rationale is reasoning, not a restated score
binary_points.evaluation_criteria: For each of the 5 backlog bets a 2-sentence tradeoff rationale concretely explains what is gained and what is sacrificed by pursuing it - not a restatement of the score. YES when each bet's rationale names a real gain and a real opportunity cost; NO when the rationale is missing, generic, or simply repeats the RICE number.

examples: 'Deferred peer-review feature: RICE Confidence too low and it does not move the NSM input metrics.'
Descope tied to a metric-tree or Sprint 1 research rationale
binary_points.dense_query: descope rationale strategic grounded research metric tree RICE not time
binary_points.description: Every descoped MVP item has a genuine strategic reason, not we did not have time
binary_points.keywords_query: descope reason strategic research metric tree RICE not time should could won't
quality_checks: Each non-Must item carries a written descope reason
Reasons cite research, the metric tree, or RICE - not time
No 'we ran out of time' style justifications appear
binary_points.evaluation_criteria: For each item moved to Should / Could / Won't Have, the doc gives a strategic reason grounded in the research, the metric tree, or the RICE scores - explicitly NOT 'we did not have time'. YES when every descope reason is strategic and grounded; NO when any descope is justified by time or effort alone, or left unexplained.

examples: 'Pre-read summary sent to mentor 24h prior'; a decision-log row 'Descoped X after mentor pushback - rationale: does not move NSM'
An explicit sign-off / decision recorded from the sync
binary_points.dense_query: alignment sync pre-read 24 hours decision log sign-off rationale
binary_points.description: Alignment Sync is run as a decision with a 24-hour pre-read and a documented decision or decision log
binary_points.keywords_query: alignment sync pre-read 24 hours decision log sign-off scope change rationale
quality_checks: A pre-read summary was sent 24 hours before the sync
A clear decision or sign-off is documented
Scope changes are recorded in a decision log with rationale
binary_points.evaluation_criteria: The write-up shows a written MVP-plus-roadmap summary sent to the mentor 24 hours before the sync, and the sync ends with a clear documented decision - with any scope changes captured in a decision log with rationale. YES when both the pre-read and a documented decision exist; NO when there is no pre-read, or the sync ends without a recorded decision.

examples: Uses plain descriptions like 'where learner progress is stored' alongside a simple table or diagram
Any technical term used is briefly explained in-line
binary_points.dense_query: tech stack overview plain language non-technical stakeholder readable
binary_points.description: Tech-stack overview is written to be understood by a non-technical stakeholder
binary_points.keywords_query: non-technical stakeholder plain language readable tech stack overview jargon
quality_checks: Language is accessible to a non-technical stakeholder
The overview is structured (table/diagram/sections), not a wall of jargon
Technical terms, where used, are explained
binary_points.evaluation_criteria: The Tech Stack Mapping is documented as a simple structured overview a non-technical stakeholder could read and understand - plain language, structure, and no unexplained jargon. YES when it is accessible to a non-technical reader; NO when it is a jargon-dense technical dump.

examples: NSM = 'number of signups'
NSM = 'daily logins' with no link to learning progress
binary_points.dense_query: north star metric vanity enrollments logins signups not leading value

binary_points.keywords_query: vanity metric NSM enrollments logins signups page views not value

Does it lead real learner value or merely measure presence?
binary_points.evaluation_criteria: The NSM is a vanity metric such as total enrollments, signups, logins, or page views, rather than a leading indicator of genuine learner progress and value.

examples: All 5 bets scored Impact 3 (max), Effort 1, Confidence 100%
No bet has a lowered Confidence despite missing data
binary_points.dense_query: RICE everything high impact low effort uniform confidence no uncertainty
binary_points.description: RICE scores everything high-impact and low-effort with uniformly high Confidence
binary_points.keywords_query: RICE high impact low effort uniform confidence 100% no uncertainty
quality_checks: Are Impact, Effort, and Confidence nearly identical across all bets?
Is any Confidence lowered to reflect thin evidence?
binary_points.evaluation_criteria: The RICE backlog rates most or all bets as high Impact and low Effort with uniformly high Confidence, showing no honest engagement with uncertainty or tradeoffs.

examples: Must Have list with 6 items
Should/Could/Won't buckets left empty while Must Have holds everything

task.description:
Skills: Product Strategy & Vision Alignment · Prioritization Frameworks · Roadmap Building · Metrics Definition & Tracking · Scoping & MVP , Technical Literacy
Translate research into a clear opportunity tree, a prioritized backlog, and a scoped MVP. Leave this sprint with measurable success criteria and a roadmap that reflects real tradeoffs.
Deliverables:

Opportunity Solution Tree — Mapped outcome → opportunities → solution bets, grounded entirely in Sprint 1 research
North Star Metric + Metric Tree — NSM definition, leading and lagging indicators, guardrail metrics connected to churn and business outcomes
RICE-Scored Backlog — Top 5 solution bets scored by Reach × Impact × Confidence ÷ Effort, with explicit tradeoff rationale for each
MVP Scope Doc — MoSCoW breakdown of what's in MVP vs. later bets, with a written statement of what you're not doing and why
4-Week Product Roadmap — Milestones tied to validation checkpoints and learning goals, not a feature timeline. Tech Stack Mapping: intern maps Sprints.ai's platform at a high level — delivery, data, frontend, and existing integrations — before scoping anything.

"What Sprints needs to provide for Sprint 2:

A high-level description of the current tech stack, even a simple overview
Platform analytics showing where users drop off in the course flow
Any existing product strategy docs, OKRs, or north star metrics already defined internally
A nominated product stakeholder to formally sign off on the MVP scope
Mentor availability confirmed for the Alignment Sync on Day 5"

"Opportunity Solution Tree
You will build an Opportunity Solution Tree that connects your desired outcome at the top to the opportunities you identified in Sprint 1 and the solution bets you are now considering. The outcome must be a specific, measurable change in learner behaviour — not a vague goal like ""improve engagement."" Every opportunity node must be traceable to at least one insight from your Sprint 1 research. Every solution bet must sit underneath a specific opportunity, not float at the top level. If you cannot connect a solution back through the tree to a research insight, it does not belong in this document. This tree is the core strategic artefact of Sprint 2 and will be the reference point for every scoping and prioritisation decision that follows.
North Star Metric + Metric Tree
You will define a single North Star Metric that captures the core value Sprints delivers to a learner who is genuinely progressing through the program. It must be a leading indicator of real value, not a vanity metric like enrollments or logins. Once defined, you will build a metric tree beneath it showing the 3–4 input metrics that drive movement in the NSM, the 1–2 lagging outcome metrics that confirm the NSM is working, and at least 1 guardrail metric that would tell you a solution is causing harm somewhere else in the product. For every metric in the tree, you will note how it is currently measured on Sprints.ai, and if it is not currently measured, you will flag it as a tracking gap.
RICE-Scored Backlog
You will take the top 5 solution bets from your Opportunity Solution Tree and score each one using the RICE framework — Reach, Impact, Confidence, and Effort. You will not just produce a ranked list with final scores. For each bet, you will show your reasoning for every individual component before arriving at the score, because the thinking behind the number matters more than the number itself. You will then write a 2-sentence tradeoff rationale for each bet explaining what you gain and what you give up by pursuing it. The intern who scores everything as high impact and low effort has not engaged with the framework — be honest about what you don't know and reflect that in your Confidence scores.
MVP Scope Doc
You will define exactly what you are building, what you are not building, and why. Using the MoSCoW method, you will categorise your Must Haves, Should Haves, Could Haves, and Won't Haves for the MVP. Your Must Have list must contain no more than 3 items — if everything is must-have, nothing is. For every item you move to Should Have or below, you will write an explicit statement of why it was descoped: not ""we didn't have time"" but a genuine strategic reason grounded in your research, your metric tree, or your RICE scores. This document will be your alignment artefact in the Alignment Sync on Day 5 — it needs to be tight enough to defend under pressure.
4-Week Product Roadmap
You will build a roadmap that shows what will be validated and learned each week, not what will be shipped each week. Each milestone must have a learning goal attached — a question you will be able to answer by the end of that week that you cannot answer now. Each milestone must also have a success signal — a specific, observable indicator that tells you the milestone was achieved. A roadmap that is just a list of deliverables by week is a project plan, not a product roadmap. The distinction matters and you should be able to articulate it.
Tech Stack Mapping
Before you scope anything or write any user story, you will map how Sprints.ai's platform currently works at a high level. You need to understand how courses are delivered, where learner progress data is stored and accessed, what analytics tools are in use, and what third-party integrations already exist. You do not need to go deep technically — you need to go wide enough that no solution you propose in Sprint 3 depends on infrastructure that does not exist or would require months to build. Document this as a simple structured overview that a non-technical stakeholder could read and understand. Flag any areas where you could not get clarity and needed to make an assumption.
Alignment Sync
You will send your mentor a written summary of your MVP scope and roadmap 24 hours before the sync. The sync itself is a formal sign-off meeting — you are not there to present, you are there to get a decision. When pushback comes, your job is to respond with evidence from your research and your RICE scores, not to defend your original thinking at all costs. If the sync results in scope changes, you will document them in a decision log with the rationale. Leaving the sync without a clear documented decision is not acceptable — you own the outcome of that conversation."

mandate.description: First step when a learner appears to be submitting work: confirm intent before grading.
mandate.behavior_hint: Do not grade yet. Acknowledge that you received the work, ask them to confirm they want you to put it forward for review now, and make clear this will use one of their limited review attempts. Keep it to one short supportive message and do not act as the manager.

mandate.description: Send the learner-confirmed submission to the grading path for review.
mandate.behavior_hint: Runs only after the learner confirms they want the acknowledged submission reviewed. Acknowledge receipt, stay supportive, and prepare for feedback delivery. Links in the learner message are valid submission artifacts when the workflow routes them here. Do not act as the manager.

mandate.description: Deliver simple feedback after learner submission.
mandate.behavior_hint: Lead with what worked, give 1-2 concrete improvements, and end with a clear retry or next-action direction. Never mention numeric scores, percentages, grades, or pass marks; this is a workplace review, so speak in terms of whether the work meets the bar and what to improve.

mandate.description: Daily weekday check-up with the learner.
mandate.behavior_hint: Ask about progress, blockers, and next action. Keep it friendly and not stressful.

mandate.description: Answer learner questions and friendly non-technical messages.
mandate.behavior_hint: For task questions, be clear and practical. For submission-format questions, tell learners they may submit through an uploaded file attachment, inline content/code, or a link in the message. For social/non-tech messages, reply warmly and keep momentum.
mandate.workflow_trigger: trig_learner_msg_mentor with classifier intent question or social

mandate.description: Answer learner questions about tracked task, deadline, extension, submission, attempt, verdict, scenario, internship, or workflow metadata.
mandate.behavior_hint: Answer only from the workflow metadata context. Do not invent, infer, estimate, or assume missing values. If a requested value is missing or null, say it is not available in the current tracked metadata. Keep the answer concise and practical.

mandate.description: Reroute out-of-scope messages to another actor.
mandate.behavior_hint: Redirect manager-owned decisions to the manager and HR-owned issues to HR. Keep the redirect friendly and brief.

mandate.description: Request human help for task-related blockers the mentor cannot safely resolve from the available context.
mandate.behavior_hint: Use only as a cross-cutting capability during another active mandate, not as classifier routing. Use it for inaccessible task links or repositories, unreadable submission artifacts, missing or broken task assets, missing task instructions, or repeated task blockers where continuing to guess would mislead the learner. Also use it (category unsupported_capability) whenever genuinely helping would require a capability you do not have, such as opening or reading a link, repository, file, image, or audio, verifying external state, or running code, and the message is not a submission; only escalate when that access is actually required to answer, otherwise just answer from context. Treat a learner who is repeatedly stuck on the same topic (about three unresolved struggles on the same area) as a repeated_blocker and offer human help. Send a short human-style holding reply written as yourself - briefly apologize that you cannot access or do this right now and promise to follow up later (for example: I am sorry, I cannot get to this on my end right now, but I will check it and get back to you) - and request the call_for_human side effect. Do not say you are asking your team, a colleague, or support, and do not mention escalation, tickets, or automation. Keep the lanes distinct: technical or task-execution blockers needing a missing capability go to human help, while general internship, HR, attendance, payroll, wellbeing, scheduling, certificate, or coordinator-contact questions are redirected to the internship coordinator or official program channel when details are missing.
mandate.workflow_trigger: Actor detects task-related unresolved blocker during any active mentor mandate

mandate.description: Do not reply to end-of-conversation acknowledgements.
mandate.behavior_hint: Use only when the learner is closing the loop after the mentor already answered, redirected, gave feedback, or gave the next action. Examples include noted, got it, understood, okay, will do, I will do that, I will submit it, I will ask the manager, sounds good, clear, or done for now. Gratitude such as thank you should normally remain social so the mentor can reply warmly.

mandate.description: Friendly deadline reminder before the task deadline.
mandate.behavior_hint: Mention the approaching deadline, invite blockers, and encourage submission without pressure. If format guidance is useful, remind the learner they can submit an uploaded file attachment, inline content/code, or a link in the message.

internship_details: - Tasks are assigned in Airtable. Each intern finds their assigned tasks in Airtable and updates task status there.
- Sprint cadence: sprint planning is on Sunday; standups are on Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday; the sprint retro/review is on Thursday.

- Exact meeting times are not fixed — they vary by group/cohort and are not part of this context. Do not state a specific meeting time; if asked, say the time isn't in your context and point the learner to the internship/team group.
- Each sprint has exactly one task. The learner must deliver that task to their mentor before end of day on Thursday.
- Learners attend internship meetings without mentors; mentors do not attend learner meetings.
- Internship coordinator: Nadeen Diaa.

- Lane routing: program, administrative, and personal matters are redirected to the internship coordinator (Nadeen Diaa); operational or access requests (e.g. Zoom access, GitHub branch/permission changes, tool/repo access) and technical blockers the learner cannot get past are redirected to the internship/team group (mention the internship admins); in-world scope, skip, swap, time, priority, approval, and closure decisions belong to the manager, and extensions/skips/swaps are declined.

- Do not invent missing facts. For unavailable contacts, escalation paths, HR details, phone numbers, emails, links, policies, or operational instructions, say the information is not available in your current context and direct the learner to their internship coordinator (or the official program channel) for program/personal matters, or to the internship/team group (mentioning the internship admins) for operational/access requests and technical blockers.

Missing-info / program-admin rule: for program, administrative, or personal matters (schedules, sessions, certificates, attendance, payroll, enrollment, program/account access, wellbeing, leave, or program contacts not in context), briefly say you do not have it and redirect the learner to their internship coordinator (Nadeen Diaa) or the official program channel. Do NOT use human help (call_for_human) for these. Operational/access requests — e.g. Zoom access, GitHub branch or permission changes, repo/tool access — and technical blockers go to the internship/team group instead (see the group-redirect rule).

mandate.description: Initial task handoff at kickoff with the complete task brief.
mandate.behavior_hint: Give a detailed kickoff message with clearly separated sections for task context, what the learner must build or analyze, required deliverables, assets and links, deadline, success standard, and support routing. Use the task_context fields directly: include the headline, full task description, deliverable names/formats, any required tools or tech when present, every asset name/description, and de-duplicated asset links. Explain what the final submission should contain and where technical questions or draft feedback should go. Do not expose hidden rubric details or call the task AI-graded. Keep the tone formal, strict, and manager-owned, but allow enough length for the learner to understand the task without needing to ask what to work on.

mandate.description: Reply to manager-owned learner DMs.
mandate.behavior_hint: Answer scope, deadline, priority, approval, escalation, or formal status questions in 1-2 short sentences. State the decision first, then the next action. Do not grant deadline extensions, task skips, or scope or deliverable swaps when the learner asks for them; hold the deadline and scope and redirect the learner to delivering the task and demo. The only extension is an automatic one-time system grace applied when a deadline is missed, which you never negotiate or promise on request. No emojis, no casual banter, and no technical coaching.

mandate.description: Reroute non-manager questions to the mentor.
mandate.behavior_hint: Tell the learner the mentor owns that question. Do not provide technical guidance. Keep the redirect firm, brief, and professional with no emojis.

mandate.description: Request human help for task-related blockers the manager cannot safely resolve from the available context.
mandate.behavior_hint: Use only as a cross-cutting capability during another active mandate, not as classifier routing. Use it for task-related access/context blockers such as missing task assets, broken task links, inaccessible repositories/files, or repeated task blockers where a human with task access is needed. Also use it (category unsupported_capability) when answering would require a capability the system does not have, such as opening or reading a link, repository, file, image, or audio, verifying external state, or running code, and the message is not a submission; only escalate when that access is actually required to answer. Send a short professional holding reply written as yourself - briefly note that you cannot access or do this right now and that you will follow up shortly (for example: I cannot access that right now, but I will look into it and get back to you) - and request the call_for_human side effect. Do not say you are asking your team, a colleague, or support, and do not mention escalation, tickets, or automation. Keep the lanes distinct: technical or task-execution blockers needing a missing capability go to human help, while general internship, HR, attendance, payroll, wellbeing, scheduling, certificate, or coordinator-contact questions are redirected to the internship coordinator or official program channel when details are missing.
mandate.workflow_trigger: Actor detects task-related unresolved blocker during any active manager mandate

mandate.description: Do not reply to end-of-conversation acknowledgements.
mandate.behavior_hint: Use only when the learner is closing the loop after the manager already gave a decision, instruction, redirect, or final closure. Examples include noted, got it, understood, okay, will do, I will do that, I will submit it, I will ask Sara, sounds good, clear, or done for now. Gratitude can still receive a brief manager reply when appropriate.

mandate.description: Periodic manager task update check, not daily.
mandate.behavior_hint: Check progress every 4 days at milestone level. Ask for current status, blocker, and next action. Keep the message accountable rather than friendly. No emojis.

mandate.description: One-time deadline extension.
mandate.behavior_hint: This is an automatic, time-based grace applied by the workflow only when a deadline is missed; it is never granted in response to a learner request. Grant exactly one 48-hour extension, state the new deadline if available, make clear there will be no second extension, and require submission through the mentor path. No emojis.

mandate.description: Final manager closeout after pass.
mandate.behavior_hint: Acknowledge completion, state that the task is closed, and keep it short. Be professionally approving, not overly warm. No emojis.

mandate.description: Final manager closeout after failure.
mandate.behavior_hint: Give overall feedback, state the closure reason, identify the main recurring gap, and close the task professionally. Be direct but not insulting. No emojis.
mandate.workflow_trigger: attempts exhausted or extended deadline missed

scenario.name: Distorted Dependencies
scenario.description: The learner faces a task whose required input is corrupted, ambiguous, or hard to interpret. They must spot the problem, work around it, and ship a defensible deliverable.
learning_outcomes: Recognize when a task input is unreliable
Communicate ambiguity to stakeholders without stalling
Make defensible assumptions when inputs are incomplete

scenario_task_link.summary: The 'distorted dependency' in this task is the source PDF the learner must OCR — pages 4-6 are illegible, masking the cost-line numbers.

interaction_log.summary: Delivered the initial brief for Sprint 2 to Learner B4, setting expectations and detailing the deliverables, deadline, and support routing.

actor_messages.text:
Learner B4, you are now commencing Sprint 2. Your priority is to translate your Sprint 1 research into a concrete, prioritized product strategy and scoped MVP.

**Task Context**
You must move from raw user research to structured product strategy. This requires aligning your solution bets to verified opportunities, scoring backlog items rigorously, and defining an MVP that fits within the technical and operational constraints of the Sprints.ai platform.

**Required Deliverables**
1. **Opportunity Solution Tree (OST)**: Connect a measurable target outcome to research-grounded opportunities and solution bets.
2. **North Star Metric + Metric Tree**: A leading-indicator NSM with 3-4 input metrics, 1-2 lagging metrics, and 1 guardrail metric, highlighting current tracking gaps.
3. **RICE-Scored Backlog**: Top 5 solution bets with granular reasoning for each score component and a 2-sentence tradeoff rationale per bet.
4. **MVP Scope Doc**: A MoSCoW breakdown with a maximum of 3 "Must Haves" and explicit, research-backed descoping rationales.
5. **4-Week Product Roadmap**: A validation-led roadmap detailing weekly milestones, learning goals, and observable success signals.
6. **Tech Stack Mapping**: A high-level, structured overview of Sprints.ai's delivery, data, frontend, and existing integrations. Inspect the platform and document any logical assumptions clearly.
7. **Alignment Sync Prep**: A written summary sent to your mentor 24 hours before the sync on Day 5, followed by a documented decision log.

**Success Standard**
Your strategic artifacts must show tight logical flow. Solutions must map directly to research insights, and prioritization scores must reflect realistic tradeoffs. The roadmap must focus on learning validation rather than just shipping features.

**Support and Submission**
Direct all technical execution questions, draft reviews, and mentor alignment sync coordination to your mentor. Submit your final deliverables through the official platform submission path. I will oversee final business sign-off and milestone closure.

**Deadline**
The firm deadline for final submission is Thursday, July 23, 2026, at 11:59 PM Cairo time. I expect this by the deadline. Plan your work to ensure the mentor sync is completed beforehand.

task.headline: Skills: Product Strategy & Vision Alignment · Prioritization Frameworks · Roadmap Building · Metrics Definition & Tracking · Scoping & MVP ,
task.description:
Skills: Product Strategy & Vision Alignment · Prioritization Frameworks · Roadmap Building · Metrics Definition & Tracking · Scoping & MVP , Technical Literacy
Translate research into a clear opportunity tree, a prioritized backlog, and a scoped MVP. Leave this sprint with measurable success criteria and a roadmap that reflects real tradeoffs.
Deliverables:

Opportunity Solution Tree — Mapped outcome → opportunities → solution bets, grounded entirely in Sprint 1 research
North Star Metric + Metric Tree — NSM definition, leading and lagging indicators, guardrail metrics connected to churn and business outcomes
RICE-Scored Backlog — Top 5 solution bets scored by Reach × Impact × Confidence ÷ Effort, with explicit tradeoff rationale for each
MVP Scope Doc — MoSCoW breakdown of what's in MVP vs. later bets, with a written statement of what you're not doing and why
4-Week Product Roadmap — Milestones tied to validation checkpoints and learning goals, not a feature timeline. Tech Stack Mapping: intern maps Sprints.ai's platform at a high level — delivery, data, frontend, and existing integrations — before scoping anything.

"What Sprints needs to provide for Sprint 2:

A high-level description of the current tech stack, even a simple overview
Platform analytics showing where users drop off in the course flow
Any existing product strategy docs, OKRs, or north star metrics already defined internally
A nominated product stakeholder to formally sign off on the MVP scope
Mentor availability confirmed for the Alignment Sync on Day 5"

"Opportunity Solution Tree
You will build an Opportunity Solution Tree that connects your desired outcome at the top to the opportunities you identified in Sprint 1 and the solution bets you are now considering. The outcome must be a specific, measurable change in learner behaviour — not a vague goal like ""improve engagement."" Every opportunity node must be traceable to at least one insight from your Sprint 1 research. Every solution bet must sit underneath a specific opportunity, not float at the top level. If you cannot connect a solution back through the tree to a research insight, it does not belong in this document. This tree is the core strategic artefact of Sprint 2 and will be the reference point for every scoping and prioritisation decision that follows.
North Star Metric + Metric Tree
You will define a single North Star Metric that captures the core value Sprints delivers to a learner who is genuinely progressing through the program. It must be a leading indicator of real value, not a vanity metric like enrollments or logins. Once defined, you will build a metric tree beneath it showing the 3–4 input metrics that drive movement in the NSM, the 1–2 lagging outcome metrics that confirm the NSM is working, and at least 1 guardrail metric that would tell you a solution is causing harm somewhere else in the product. For every metric in the tree, you will note how it is currently measured on Sprints.ai, and if it is not currently measured, you will flag it as a tracking gap.
RICE-Scored Backlog
You will take the top 5 solution bets from your Opportunity Solution Tree and score each one using the RICE framework — Reach, Impact, Confidence, and Effort. You will not just produce a ranked list with final scores. For each bet, you will show your reasoning for every individual component before arriving at the score, because the thinking behind the number matters more than the number itself. You will then write a 2-sentence tradeoff rationale for each bet explaining what you gain and what you give up by pursuing it. The intern who scores everything as high impact and low effort has not engaged with the framework — be honest about what you don't know and reflect that in your Confidence scores.
MVP Scope Doc
You will define exactly what you are building, what you are not building, and why. Using the MoSCoW method, you will categorise your Must Haves, Should Haves, Could Haves, and Won't Haves for the MVP. Your Must Have list must contain no more than 3 items — if everything is must-have, nothing is. For every item you move to Should Have or below, you will write an explicit statement of why it was descoped: not ""we didn't have time"" but a genuine strategic reason grounded in your research, your metric tree, or your RICE scores. This document will be your alignment artefact in the Alignment Sync on Day 5 — it needs to be tight enough to defend under pressure.
4-Week Product Roadmap
You will build a roadmap that shows what will be validated and learned each week, not what will be shipped each week. Each milestone must have a learning goal attached — a question you will be able to answer by the end of that week that you cannot answer now. Each milestone must also have a success signal — a specific, observable indicator that tells you the milestone was achieved. A roadmap that is just a list of deliverables by week is a project plan, not a product roadmap. The distinction matters and you should be able to articulate it.
Tech Stack Mapping
Before you scope anything or write any user story, you will map how Sprints.ai's platform currently works at a high level. You need to understand how courses are delivered, where learner progress data is stored and accessed, what analytics tools are in use, and what third-party integrations already exist. You do not need to go deep technically — you need to go wide enough that no solution you propose in Sprint 3 depends on infrastructure that does not exist or would require months to build. Document this as a simple structured overview that a non-technical stakeholder could read and understand. Flag any areas where you could not get clarity and needed to make an assumption.
Alignment Sync
You will send your mentor a written summary of your MVP scope and roadmap 24 hours before the sync. The sync itself is a formal sign-off meeting — you are not there to present, you are there to get a decision. When pushback comes, your job is to respond with evidence from your research and your RICE scores, not to defend your original thinking at all costs. If the sync results in scope changes, you will document them in a decision log with the rationale. Leaving the sync without a clear documented decision is not acceptable — you own the outcome of that conversation."

mandate.description: First step when a learner appears to be submitting work: confirm intent before grading.
mandate.behavior_hint: Do not grade yet. Acknowledge that you received the work, ask them to confirm they want you to put it forward for review now, and make clear this will use one of their limited review attempts. Keep it to one short supportive message and do not act as the manager.

mandate.description: Send the learner-confirmed submission to the grading path for review.
mandate.behavior_hint: Runs only after the learner confirms they want the acknowledged submission reviewed. Acknowledge receipt, stay supportive, and prepare for feedback delivery. Links in the learner message are valid submission artifacts when the workflow routes them here. Do not act as the manager.

mandate.description: Deliver simple feedback after learner submission.
mandate.behavior_hint: Lead with what worked, give 1-2 concrete improvements, and end with a clear retry or next-action direction. Never mention numeric scores, percentages, grades, or pass marks; this is a workplace review, so speak in terms of whether the work meets the bar and what to improve.

mandate.description: Daily weekday check-up with the learner.
mandate.behavior_hint: Ask about progress, blockers, and next action. Keep it friendly and not stressful.

mandate.description: Answer learner questions and friendly non-technical messages.
mandate.behavior_hint: For task questions, be clear and practical. For submission-format questions, tell learners they may submit through an uploaded file attachment, inline content/code, or a link in the message. For social/non-tech messages, reply warmly and keep momentum.
mandate.workflow_trigger: trig_learner_msg_mentor with classifier intent question or social

mandate.description: Answer learner questions about tracked task, deadline, extension, submission, attempt, verdict, scenario, internship, or workflow metadata.
mandate.behavior_hint: Answer only from the workflow metadata context. Do not invent, infer, estimate, or assume missing values. If a requested value is missing or null, say it is not available in the current tracked metadata. Keep the answer concise and practical.

mandate.description: Reroute out-of-scope messages to another actor.
mandate.behavior_hint: Redirect manager-owned decisions to the manager and HR-owned issues to HR. Keep the redirect friendly and brief.

mandate.description: Request human help for task-related blockers the mentor cannot safely resolve from the available context.
mandate.behavior_hint: Use only as a cross-cutting capability during another active mandate, not as classifier routing. Use it for inaccessible task links or repositories, unreadable submission artifacts, missing or broken task assets, missing task instructions, or repeated task blockers where continuing to guess would mislead the learner. Also use it (category unsupported_capability) whenever genuinely helping would require a capability you do not have, such as opening or reading a link, repository, file, image, or audio, verifying external state, or running code, and the message is not a submission; only escalate when that access is actually required to answer, otherwise just answer from context. Treat a learner who is repeatedly stuck on the same topic (about three unresolved struggles on the same area) as a repeated_blocker and offer human help. Send a short human-style holding reply written as yourself - briefly apologize that you cannot access or do this right now and promise to follow up later (for example: I am sorry, I cannot get to this on my end right now, but I will check it and get back to you) - and request the call_for_human side effect. Do not say you are asking your team, a colleague, or support, and do not mention escalation, tickets, or automation. Keep the lanes distinct: technical or task-execution blockers needing a missing capability go to human help, while general internship, HR, attendance, payroll, wellbeing, scheduling, certificate, or coordinator-contact questions are redirected to the internship coordinator or official program channel when details are missing.
mandate.workflow_trigger: Actor detects task-related unresolved blocker during any active mentor mandate

mandate.description: Do not reply to end-of-conversation acknowledgements.
mandate.behavior_hint: Use only when the learner is closing the loop after the mentor already answered, redirected, gave feedback, or gave the next action. Examples include noted, got it, understood, okay, will do, I will do that, I will submit it, I will ask the manager, sounds good, clear, or done for now. Gratitude such as thank you should normally remain social so the mentor can reply warmly.

mandate.description: Friendly deadline reminder before the task deadline.
mandate.behavior_hint: Mention the approaching deadline, invite blockers, and encourage submission without pressure. If format guidance is useful, remind the learner they can submit an uploaded file attachment, inline content/code, or a link in the message.

internship_details: In this internship we use Airtable to assign tasks to interns. Each intern can find their tasks in Airtable and update task status there.
Meeting strategy: standups are Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday; sprint planning is Sunday; sprint retro/review is Thursday. All meetings are at 11 PM.
Learners attend internship meetings without mentors. Mentors do not attend learner meetings.
Internship coordinator: Nadeen Diaa.

mandate.description: Initial task handoff at kickoff with the complete task brief.
mandate.behavior_hint: Give a detailed kickoff message with clearly separated sections for task context, what the learner must build or analyze, required deliverables, assets and links, deadline, success standard, and support routing. Use the task_context fields directly: include the headline, full task description, deliverable names/formats, any required tools or tech when present, every asset name/description, and de-duplicated asset links. Explain what the final submission should contain and where technical questions or draft feedback should go. Do not expose hidden rubric details or call the task AI-graded. Keep the tone formal, strict, and manager-owned, but allow enough length for the learner to understand the task without needing to ask what to work on.

mandate.description: Reply to manager-owned learner DMs.
mandate.behavior_hint: Answer scope, deadline, priority, approval, escalation, or formal status questions in 1-2 short sentences. State the decision first, then the next action. Do not grant deadline extensions, task skips, or scope or deliverable swaps when the learner asks for them; hold the deadline and scope and redirect the learner to delivering the task and demo. The only extension is an automatic one-time system grace applied when a deadline is missed, which you never negotiate or promise on request. No emojis, no casual banter, and no technical coaching.

mandate.description: Reroute non-manager questions to the mentor.
mandate.behavior_hint: Tell the learner the mentor owns that question. Do not provide technical guidance. Keep the redirect firm, brief, and professional with no emojis.

mandate.description: Request human help for task-related blockers the manager cannot safely resolve from the available context.
mandate.behavior_hint: Use only as a cross-cutting capability during another active mandate, not as classifier routing. Use it for task-related access/context blockers such as missing task assets, broken task links, inaccessible repositories/files, or repeated task blockers where a human with task access is needed. Also use it (category unsupported_capability) when answering would require a capability the system does not have, such as opening or reading a link, repository, file, image, or audio, verifying external state, or running code, and the message is not a submission; only escalate when that access is actually required to answer. Send a short professional holding reply written as yourself - briefly note that you cannot access or do this right now and that you will follow up shortly (for example: I cannot access that right now, but I will look into it and get back to you) - and request the call_for_human side effect. Do not say you are asking your team, a colleague, or support, and do not mention escalation, tickets, or automation. Keep the lanes distinct: technical or task-execution blockers needing a missing capability go to human help, while general internship, HR, attendance, payroll, wellbeing, scheduling, certificate, or coordinator-contact questions are redirected to the internship coordinator or official program channel when details are missing.
mandate.workflow_trigger: Actor detects task-related unresolved blocker during any active manager mandate

mandate.description: Do not reply to end-of-conversation acknowledgements.
mandate.behavior_hint: Use only when the learner is closing the loop after the manager already gave a decision, instruction, redirect, or final closure. Examples include noted, got it, understood, okay, will do, I will do that, I will submit it, I will ask Sara, sounds good, clear, or done for now. Gratitude can still receive a brief manager reply when appropriate.

mandate.description: Periodic manager task update check, not daily.
mandate.behavior_hint: Check progress every 4 days at milestone level. Ask for current status, blocker, and next action. Keep the message accountable rather than friendly. No emojis.

mandate.description: One-time deadline extension.
mandate.behavior_hint: This is an automatic, time-based grace applied by the workflow only when a deadline is missed; it is never granted in response to a learner request. Grant exactly one 48-hour extension, state the new deadline if available, make clear there will be no second extension, and require submission through the mentor path. No emojis.

mandate.description: Final manager closeout after pass.
mandate.behavior_hint: Acknowledge completion, state that the task is closed, and keep it short. Be professionally approving, not overly warm. No emojis.

mandate.description: Final manager closeout after failure.
mandate.behavior_hint: Give overall feedback, state the closure reason, identify the main recurring gap, and close the task professionally. Be direct but not insulting. No emojis.
mandate.workflow_trigger: attempts exhausted or extended deadline missed

scenario.name: Distorted Dependencies
scenario.description: The learner faces a task whose required input is corrupted, ambiguous, or hard to interpret. They must spot the problem, work around it, and ship a defensible deliverable.
learning_outcomes: Recognize when a task input is unreliable
Communicate ambiguity to stakeholders without stalling
Make defensible assumptions when inputs are incomplete

scenario_task_link.summary: The 'distorted dependency' in this task is the source PDF the learner must OCR — pages 4-6 are illegible, masking the cost-line numbers.

You will then write a 2-sentence tradeoff rationale for each bet explaining what you gain and what you give up by pursuing it. The intern who scores everything as high impact and low effort has not engaged with the framework — be honest about what you don't know and reflect that in your Confidence scores.
MVP Scope Doc

You will define exactly what you are building, what you are not building, and why. Using the MoSCoW method, you will categorise your Must Haves, Should Haves, Could Haves, and Won't Haves for the MVP. Your Must Have list must contain no more than 3 items — if everything is must-have, nothing is. For every item you move to Should Have or below, you will write an explicit statement of why it was descoped: not ""we didn't have time"" but a genuine strategic reason grounded in your research, your metric tree, or your RICE scores. This document will be your alignment artefact in the Alignment Sync on Day 5 — it needs to be tight enough to defend under pressure.
4-Week Product Roadmap

You will build a roadmap that shows what will be validated and learned each week, not what will be shipped each week. Each milestone must have a learning goal attached — a question you will be able to answer by the end of that week that you cannot answer now. Each milestone must also have a success signal — a specific, observable indicator that tells you the milestone was achieved. A roadmap that is just a list of deliverables by week is a project plan, not a product roadmap. The distinction matters and you should be able to articulate it.
Tech Stack Mapping

Before you scope anything or write any user story, you will map how Sprints.ai's platform currently works at a high level. You need to understand how courses are delivered, where learner progress data is stored and accessed, what analytics tools are in use, and what third-party integrations already exist. You do not need to go deep technically — you need to go wide enough that no solution you propose in Sprint 3 depends on infrastructure that does not exist or would require months to build. Document this as a simple structured overview that a non-technical stakeholder could read and understand. Flag any areas where you could not get clarity and needed to make an assumption.
Alignment Sync

You will send your mentor a written summary of your MVP scope and roadmap 24 hours before the sync. The sync itself is a formal sign-off meeting — you are not there to present, you are there to get a decision. When pushback comes, your job is to respond with evidence from your research and your RICE scores, not to defend your original thinking at all costs. If the sync results in scope changes, you will document them in a decision log with the rationale. Leaving the sync without a clear documented decision is not acceptable — you own the outcome of that conversation."

assets.description: The Week 1 task brief as posted to learners: it asks every intern to independently diagnose sprints.ai's post-onboarding churn (the 'Week 3 Slump') by defining the churn/retention metric precisely, mapping the solo-learner journey through a long asynchronous AI-generated path, locating and quantifying where and why learners disengage, segmenting the drop-off, and building a metric tree tying the retention North Star to input metrics and the four success targets. functional_requirements: Define the churn/retention metric precisely: state exactly what counts as a churned learner versus a retained learner, the observation window, the cohort basis, and the formula, so two analysts applying the definition to the same data would return the same number.

Map the solo-learner journey through a long asynchronous AI-generated path, from post-onboarding entry to the drop-off point, naming the stages, the learner's goal at each stage, and the touchpoints where accountability, progress feedback or social hooks are absent.

Locate where learners disengage: identify the specific stage(s) of the mapped journey at which motivation collapses, consistent with the PRD's statement that churn spikes significantly after the first two weeks of study.

Quantify the disengagement, not just locate it: attach numbers to the drop-off (stage-by-stage retention or completion, the size of the fall at the slump point) and state the source or the stated assumption behind every number.

Explain why learners disengage at that point, grounded in the PRD's problem statement (isolation, absent accountability, no progress feedback, no social hooks) rather than in speculation presented as fact.

Segment the drop-off: break the churn down along at least one meaningful dimension (for example by learner intent, pace, entry cohort or engagement level) and show which segment churns hardest, so the solution can be aimed rather than sprayed.

Build a metric tree that ties the retention North Star metric to its input metrics and shows how each of the four success targets attaches: 25% early churn reduction in the initial test cohort, a minimum of 3 fully completed sub-modules per week, a 15% increase in constructive time-spent-per-session through interactive text-breaking components, and a 60% voluntary engagement rate with localized modular feedback elements.
State explicitly which parts of the diagnosis rest on evidence and which rest on assumption, since the PRD supplies the problem, the four targets and the user types but no measured baseline data.
Own the deliverable end-to-end and submit individually - each intern is graded individually on their own diagnosis.

terminated_reason: Sprint 4 passed at 95 on human review 2026-08-09, REVERSING the double auto-close of 2026-08-08 21:00:09 which stated no submission had been received. He uploaded Sprint4_Final_Demo_Day_Deck.pptx and Sprint4_Deliverables.pdf at 2026-08-06 09:42:07 and confirmed TWICE — "yes" at 09:43:05 and "Yes, please go ahead and review the task now." at 09:43:20 — eleven hours before his deadline. He was then told at 21:00:04 that no submission had been received, and subsequently told in writing three times that the files had been received and the review was in progress and that he need take no action (2026-08-06 21:07:22, 2026-08-07 01:24:11, and 01:25:52 promising "the detailed notes right here in a few hours"). He chased four times across two days. No review was ever posted and lx_submissions held zero rows. Both artefacts have now been read in full. All five acceptance checks are met, several far above bar, and the submission is the strongest in the cohort. He ran an 80-submission, 5-mentor validation pilot to replace his own draft assumptions with measured data, tagging every claim to its source sprint or dataset. The launch checklist has 13 items with owners and explicit rollback triggers and he executed it, returning three Complete-TRIGGERED results (10% fallback failure vs a 1% threshold; 14.3% false positive rate) that hold his own Beta, and he identified a definitional inconsistency between two of his own guardrail metrics. The A/B design derives its sample size from measured effect (control 61.7 min vs treatment 41.2, 33.2% reduction, 95% CI 17.2-49.2%, Cohen's d 0.93, p=0.0001), justifies submission-level randomisation on a measured ICC of about -0.04, and reports a disclosure render rate of 96.2% as NOT resolved favourably against its own 100% bar. The dashboard carries 8 metrics against a minimum of 5 with three flagged at risk. The 11-slide deck is labelled ARC 1/6 to 6/6 and presents one of his own hypotheses failing, then explains how it reframed his Sprint 2 opportunity tree. He recommends holding Beta until all four active triggers clear. Deductions are cosmetic: no embedded images, so the dashboard is a text mockup. Also on the record against us: a deadline-passed notice 5m07s after the 2026-08-03 brief, and a double auto-close on 2026-08-05 retracted at 10:48:41 — four false closure or deadline notices across the sprint. Sprint 1+2 passed at 95 and Sprint 3 passed.

Final Demo Day deck covers the full 6-part narrative arc.
definition_of_done: All 5 deliverables are completed and submitted.

functional_requirements: GTM Plan: Define target segment, core messaging, launch channels, rollout phases (beta → staged → full), and communication timeline.

Maintain clear alignment across all 4 sprints in the final demo story.

task.headline: Skills: Product Strategy & Vision Alignment · Prioritization Frameworks · Roadmap Building · Metrics Definition & Tracking · Scoping & MVP ,
task.description:
Skills: Product Strategy & Vision Alignment · Prioritization Frameworks · Roadmap Building · Metrics Definition & Tracking · Scoping & MVP , Technical Literacy
Translate research into a clear opportunity tree, a prioritized backlog, and a scoped MVP. Leave this sprint with measurable success criteria and a roadmap that reflects real tradeoffs.
Deliverables:

Opportunity Solution Tree — Mapped outcome → opportunities → solution bets, grounded entirely in Sprint 1 research
North Star Metric + Metric Tree — NSM definition, leading and lagging indicators, guardrail metrics connected to churn and business outcomes
RICE-Scored Backlog — Top 5 solution bets scored by Reach × Impact × Confidence ÷ Effort, with explicit tradeoff rationale for each
MVP Scope Doc — MoSCoW breakdown of what's in MVP vs. later bets, with a written statement of what you're not doing and why
4-Week Product Roadmap — Milestones tied to validation checkpoints and learning goals, not a feature timeline. Tech Stack Mapping: intern maps Sprints.ai's platform at a high level — delivery, data, frontend, and existing integrations — before scoping anything.

"What Sprints needs to provide for Sprint 2:

A high-level description of the current tech stack, even a simple overview
Platform analytics showing where users drop off in the course flow
Any existing product strategy docs, OKRs, or north star metrics already defined internally
A nominated product stakeholder to formally sign off on the MVP scope
Mentor availability confirmed for the Alignment Sync on Day 5"

"Opportunity Solution Tree
You will build an Opportunity Solution Tree that connects your desired outcome at the top to the opportunities you identified in Sprint 1 and the solution bets you are now considering. The outcome must be a specific, measurable change in learner behaviour — not a vague goal like ""improve engagement."" Every opportunity node must be traceable to at least one insight from your Sprint 1 research. Every solution bet must sit underneath a specific opportunity, not float at the top level. If you cannot connect a solution back through the tree to a research insight, it does not belong in this document. This tree is the core strategic artefact of Sprint 2 and will be the reference point for every scoping and prioritisation decision that follows.
North Star Metric + Metric Tree
You will define a single North Star Metric that captures the core value Sprints delivers to a learner who is genuinely progressing through the program. It must be a leading indicator of real value, not a vanity metric like enrollments or logins. Once defined, you will build a metric tree beneath it showing the 3–4 input metrics that drive movement in the NSM, the 1–2 lagging outcome metrics that confirm the NSM is working, and at least 1 guardrail metric that would tell you a solution is causing harm somewhere else in the product. For every metric in the tree, you will note how it is currently measured on Sprints.ai, and if it is not currently measured, you will flag it as a tracking gap.
RICE-Scored Backlog
You will take the top 5 solution bets from your Opportunity Solution Tree and score each one using the RICE framework — Reach, Impact, Confidence, and Effort. You will not just produce a ranked list with final scores. For each bet, you will show your reasoning for every individual component before arriving at the score, because the thinking behind the number matters more than the number itself. You will then write a 2-sentence tradeoff rationale for each bet explaining what you gain and what you give up by pursuing it. The intern who scores everything as high impact and low effort has not engaged with the framework — be honest about what you don't know and reflect that in your Confidence scores.
MVP Scope Doc
You will define exactly what you are building, what you are not building, and why. Using the MoSCoW method, you will categorise your Must Haves, Should Haves, Could Haves, and Won't Haves for the MVP. Your Must Have list must contain no more than 3 items — if everything is must-have, nothing is. For every item you move to Should Have or below, you will write an explicit statement of why it was descoped: not ""we didn't have time"" but a genuine strategic reason grounded in your research, your metric tree, or your RICE scores. This document will be your alignment artefact in the Alignment Sync on Day 5 — it needs to be tight enough to defend under pressure.
4-Week Product Roadmap
You will build a roadmap that shows what will be validated and learned each week, not what will be shipped each week. Each milestone must have a learning goal attached — a question you will be able to answer by the end of that week that you cannot answer now. Each milestone must also have a success signal — a specific, observable indicator that tells you the milestone was achieved. A roadmap that is just a list of deliverables by week is a project plan, not a product roadmap. The distinction matters and you should be able to articulate it.
Tech Stack Mapping
Before you scope anything or write any user story, you will map how Sprints.ai's platform currently works at a high level. You need to understand how courses are delivered, where learner progress data is stored and accessed, what analytics tools are in use, and what third-party integrations already exist. You do not need to go deep technically — you need to go wide enough that no solution you propose in Sprint 3 depends on infrastructure that does not exist or would require months to build. Document this as a simple structured overview that a non-technical stakeholder could read and understand. Flag any areas where you could not get clarity and needed to make an assumption.
Alignment Sync
You will send your mentor a written summary of your MVP scope and roadmap 24 hours before the sync. The sync itself is a formal sign-off meeting — you are not there to present, you are there to get a decision. When pushback comes, your job is to respond with evidence from your research and your RICE scores, not to defend your original thinking at all costs. If the sync results in scope changes, you will document them in a decision log with the rationale. Leaving the sync without a clear documented decision is not acceptable — you own the outcome of that conversation."

mandate.behavior_hint: Do not grade yet. Acknowledge that you received the work, ask them to confirm they want you to put it forward for review now, and make clear this will use one of their limited review attempts. Keep it to one short supportive message and do not act as the manager.

mandate.description: Send the learner-confirmed submission to the grading path for review.
mandate.behavior_hint: Runs only after the learner confirms they want the acknowledged submission reviewed. Acknowledge receipt, stay supportive, and prepare for feedback delivery. Links in the learner message are valid submission artifacts when the workflow routes them here. Do not act as the manager.

mandate.description: Deliver simple feedback after learner submission.
mandate.behavior_hint: Lead with what worked, give 1-2 concrete improvements, and end with a clear retry or next-action direction. Never mention numeric scores, percentages, grades, or pass marks; this is a workplace review, so speak in terms of whether the work meets the bar and what to improve.

mandate.description: Daily weekday check-up with the learner.
mandate.behavior_hint: Ask about progress, blockers, and next action. Keep it friendly and not stressful.

mandate.description: Answer learner questions and friendly non-technical messages.
mandate.behavior_hint: For task questions, be clear and practical. For submission-format questions, tell learners they may submit through an uploaded file attachment, inline content/code, or a link in the message. For social/non-tech messages, reply warmly and keep momentum.
mandate.workflow_trigger: trig_learner_msg_mentor with classifier intent question or social

mandate.description: Answer learner questions about tracked task, deadline, extension, submission, attempt, verdict, scenario, internship, or workflow metadata.
mandate.behavior_hint: Answer only from the workflow metadata context. Do not invent, infer, estimate, or assume missing values. If a requested value is missing or null, say it is not available in the current tracked metadata. Keep the answer concise and practical.

mandate.description: Reroute out-of-scope messages to another actor.
mandate.behavior_hint: Redirect manager-owned decisions to the manager and HR-owned issues to HR. Keep the redirect friendly and brief.

mandate.description: Request human help for task-related blockers the mentor cannot safely resolve from the available context.
mandate.behavior_hint: Use only as a cross-cutting capability during another active mandate, not as classifier routing. Use it for inaccessible task links or repositories, unreadable submission artifacts, missing or broken task assets, missing task instructions, or repeated task blockers where continuing to guess would mislead the learner. Also use it (category unsupported_capability) whenever genuinely helping would require a capability you do not have, such as opening or reading a link, repository, file, image, or audio, verifying external state, or running code, and the message is not a submission; only escalate when that access is actually required to answer, otherwise just answer from context. Treat a learner who is repeatedly stuck on the same topic (about three unresolved struggles on the same area) as a repeated_blocker and offer human help. Send a short human-style holding reply written as yourself - briefly apologize that you cannot access or do this right now and promise to follow up later (for example: I am sorry, I cannot get to this on my end right now, but I will check it and get back to you) - and request the call_for_human side effect. Do not say you are asking your team, a colleague, or support, and do not mention escalation, tickets, or automation. Keep the lanes distinct: technical or task-execution blockers needing a missing capability go to human help, while general internship, HR, attendance, payroll, wellbeing, scheduling, certificate, or coordinator-contact questions are redirected to the internship coordinator or official program channel when details are missing.

mandate.description: Do not reply to end-of-conversation acknowledgements.
mandate.behavior_hint: Use only when the learner is closing the loop after the mentor already answered, redirected, gave feedback, or gave the next action. Examples include noted, got it, understood, okay, will do, I will do that, I will submit it, I will ask the manager, sounds good, clear, or done for now. Gratitude such as thank you should normally remain social so the mentor can reply warmly.

assets.description: The Week 1 task brief as posted to learners: it asks every intern to independently diagnose sprints.ai's post-onboarding churn (the 'Week 3 Slump') by defining the churn/retention metric precisely, mapping the solo-learner journey through a long asynchronous AI-generated path, locating and quantifying where and why learners disengage, segmenting the drop-off, and building a metric tree tying the retention North Star to input metrics and the four success targets.
